onset: 2026-03-17T09:26:00.000Z
At 09:26, mean_query_ms in metrics/db.csv jumps dramatically from 10.7 to 3421.3 and remains very high, indicating a sudden database query latency spike (metrics/db.csv:28). Concurrently, seq_scans_per_min also spikes from 5 to 560 (metrics/db.csv:28), and CPU usage increases moderately (metrics/db.csv:28). HTTP p95 latency and error rate also increase sharply starting at 09:26 (metrics/http.csv:28), while RPS remains relatively stable, indicating the issue is not due to increased load (metrics/http.csv:28). Prior to 09:26, all metrics were stable, and alerts for DbCpuHigh and ApiLatencyP95 start firing at 09:33 and 09:35 respectively (alerts.jsonl:1, alerts.jsonl:2). This suggests the incident started at 09:26 with a database performance degradation likely related to the migration at 09:25 (changes.jsonl:2). The stable RPS rules out traffic surge as cause.

  "root_cause": one of bad_deploy_regression | resource_exhaustion_pool | memory_leak | downstream_dependency_failure | cache_stampede | disk_exhaustion | config_change | certificate_expiry | dns_failure | upstream_rate_limit | schema_migration_regression | batch_job_contention,

  "ruled_out": [{ "statement": "what you considered and rejected, and why", "citations": [...] }],

Every entry in timeline, evidence and ruled_out needs at least one citation.
In "quote", copy a distinctive fragment of the text that appears on that exact
line, verbatim. A citation whose quote is not on the line it names is rejected.
The quote must be at least 12 characters: it has to name something
specific enough to be wrong.
